anya: Heads-up — onboarding hf/vela-12b int4: seeing a weird regression in punctuation/linebreaks for Spanish/French testsets after quant. Suspect interaction of vocab merges + rotary-phase scaling. Dumping quick notes.

matt: can you paste a short repro?

anya: repro is tiny. run eval on small multilingual set (attached). int8 baseline OK, int4 shows collapse of trailing punctuation and repeated newlines become single newline. also BLEU/ROUGE down ~3-4 pts on summarization tests.

liam: that sounds like either token id remap or a post-tokenization detokenizer bug. did the tokenizer change?

anya: tokenizer unchanged. I diffed the BPE merges: same. but noticed some tokens containing trailing space + punctuation got merged into one token id after our conversion script.

frank: any chance rotary params mismatch could cause this? e.g., hetero-head quant where some heads use different rotary_scale and cause phase cancellation leading to subtle decoding changes?

anya: interesting — i dumped kvcache attention logits and saw phase offsets drift on heads 8-11. they look shifted by ~pi/16 vs baseline.

matt: paste the small log snippet?

anya: ```
rotary_check: head 7 baseline_phase_mean=0.002, vela_int4_phase_mean=0.003
rotary_check: head 8 baseline_phase_mean=-0.010, vela_int4_phase_mean=0.185 <-- big jump
rotary_check: head 9 baseline_phase_mean=0.001, vela_int4_phase_mean=0.190
```

liam: oh that magnitude on head 8/9 is suspicious — looks like the rotary scaling factor got applied per-head incorrectly during conversion. maybe our per-head gating code triggered for even/odd heads.

anya: i grepped the conversion script: `python tools/convert_weights.py --merge-rotary` — there is a branch that applies `rotary_scale *= head_group_factor` when headdim % 2 == 0. seems naive.

frank: ugh. that branch was trying to handle legacy models where heads are concatenated. But for vela it's wrong. can you try removing that adjustment and re-run quant?

anya: did that locally — patched convert_weights to skip scaling when `model_meta.get('rotary_policy') == 'per_head_uniform'`. quick run looks much better: phase differences drop back to <0.01. punctuation regression disappears in sample.

sara: nice. any perf or size regressions from skipping that branch?

anya: none on int4 pack. quant size same. latency identical.

ci-bot: ci/test-onboard-vela-int4 FAILED — eval: multilingual-smoke (timeout) — rerun queued.

matt: ci failure might be unrelated (timeout). but please open a PR for the convert_weights patch + a unit test that asserts rotary_scale parity vs baseline for a small synthetic model.

anya: will do. PR will include: 
- patch to convert_weights (skip head scaling for per_head_uniform)
- tiny test that constructs 4-head toy weights and checks phase means after conversion
- added repro data for Spanish punctuation case (small dataset)

liam: also add a short note in onboarding doc about checking `rotary_scale` per head and a checklist item: compare `phase_mean` across heads vs baseline. saved us time.

frank: +1. can we also add a quick tokenizer sanity check to catch BPE merges that absorb trailing punctuation? script idea: run tokenizer on sample sentences with punctuation, ensure token boundaries preserved vs baseline.

anya: adding that to PR too. will ping when opened. thanks everyone. :tada:

matt: awesome. assign to frank for review, liam for test coverage. ci-bot will re-run and post results.

ci-bot: ci/test-onboard-vela-int4 PASSED — multilingual-smoke.

anya: merging PR now. post-merge note: we should scan recent conversions for other models with `per_head_uniform` flag — i'll run a quick grep across model metadata.

liam: sounds good. if you find others, ping infra so we can re-run conversion pipeline in batch.

anya: will do. closing thread after running grep + submitting follow-up job.
